Pikachu soft toy

A yellow plush Pikachu from the late-1990s Pokémon boom: a round body, stubby limbs, dot eyes with highlights, and red cheek discs.

Source
V&A: Soft toy, Pikachu, B.89-2004
Creator
Deutshe Toy GMBH (manufacturer, as the V&A spells it); Pokémon created by Satoshi Tajiri
Made
1995–1999 (V&A)
Style
Kawaii (partial fit; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Cute, friendly, playful
Evidence
Inspected the V&A photograph 2006AE8391 of object B.89-2004 (1200 × 1600 px, IIIF) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A says Pokémon was created by Satoshi Tajiri as games for Nintendo’s Game Boy in 1995, then moved to television, trading cards, and merchandise including soft toys; it calls Pikachu “probably the best known of the Pokémon creatures”. V&A B.89-2004.

The museum records a yellow nylon plush toy, 275 mm high, with black plastic eyes with white dots, cheeks of plastic discs covered in red material, and a stitched nose and mouth, manufactured in Munich. V&A B.89-2004.

Observed

  • The toy sits upright; the head is almost as wide as the body, and the arms and feet are short rounded stubs.
  • The eyes are black domes with a white highlight, set wide and low; the mouth is a small stitched wavy line under a dot nose.
  • Two bright red circles mark the cheeks.
  • The long ears end in black tips; the plush is an even lemon yellow.

Why it belongs

The face follows the kawaii formula almost exactly: wide-set highlighted dot eyes, a tiny mouth, and cheek blush. The proportions are those of the chibi baby schema.

The saturated yellow shows that the kawaii face and proportions can work without the pastel palette, in the toy and game branch of the style.

Borrow

Place dot eyes wide apart and low on the face, each with one small white highlight.

Make cheek blush a clean circle in a single warm color.
